mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when RSAFS increases > 1% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which is generally positive for equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is decreasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and the number of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over 3 months signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST increases > 5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals a favorable environment for corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when INDPRO > 12-month MA and FEDFUNDS < 1%.
